decisive_items: A 5 cm × 8 cm area of erythema and induration on the medial aspect of the right breast.
response.rationale: Postpartum breast erythema, induration, leukocytosis, and elevated inflammatory markers with no abscess are classic for puerperal mastitis; positive Streptococcus agalactiae culture supports an infectious cause but the clinical syndrome is mastitis. Elevated prolactin reflects lactation, and pituitary MRI shows no adenoma.

rejected.why: Pituitary MRI shows no discrete mass or lesion and there are no headaches/visual changes; heterogeneous gland alone does not establish adenoma.
Prolactin elevation and excessive milk are consistent with postpartum lactation and do not explain breast erythema/induration or elevated inflammatory markers.
